title: GES and NaCCA alignment
text: Aligned. Ghana Education Service and NaCCA curriculum standards. Ayeduase campus · Kumasi.

title: Authentic Montessori sequenced
text: Pedagogical continuum. Authentic Montessori, sequenced from the first work cycle to the final exam. We hold the Montessori method together with the Ghanaian curriculum: mixed-age classrooms and uninterrupted work periods on one side, National Council for Curriculum and Assessment requirements on the other. A child progresses from Crèche to Junior High without changing school.

title: Guide to children ratio
text: 1:6 — Guide to children, early years. Mixed-age environment. 3 hrs — Uninterrupted work cycle. Self-directed, no bells. 2 — Languages from the start. English and Asante Twi.

title: Novastar Journey to BECE
text: The Novastar Journey. A continuous path to BECE. Crèche 6mo – 2yrs. Nursery 2 – 4yrs. Kindergarten 4 – 6yrs. Primary 6 – 12yrs. Junior High 12 – 15yrs.

title: Five prepared environments
text: Five prepared environments. Each room is built with materials that isolate one kind of work, so a child can begin at any point and still find a task that holds their attention.

title: Practical Life environment
text: Practical life — First plane · the absorbent mind. Order, concentration and independence. The earliest work in a Montessori classroom is not academic. Children pour, carry, sweep, dress themselves and prepare food, because every one of those exercises trains the sustained concentration that everything later depends on. Self-care and dressing frames: Buttons, laces and zips practised on frames until the sequence needs no thought. Care of the environment: Water carried, surfaces polished, flowers watered — real responsibility, not pretend. Grace and courtesy: Turn-taking, quiet movement and shared meals practised as a form of consideration. Language through song: Nomenclature, songs and oral work before anything is expected on paper. Schedule: Uninterrupted work cycle, three terms per academic year.

title: Sensorial environment
text: Sensorial — First plane · the absorbent mind. A precise, self-correcting language for the senses. Each material isolates one sensation — colour, weight, form, texture — and contains its own error control, so a child can tell alone whether the work is right. Geometric solids and puzzles: Form and volume made visible through solids that only fit one way round. The colour and weight boxes: Gradations narrow enough to demand deliberate attention rather than guessing. Sorting and seriation: Order discovered by touch, then confirmed by eye. Care of the apparatus: Every material returned in condition, which is the discipline the work teaches. Schedule: Materials renewed seasonally at each break.

title: Mathematics environment
text: Mathematics — Second plane · the reasoning mind. From counting beads to abstract proof. Mathematics is introduced as a concrete fact the child manipulates, not a symbol the child is asked to accept. Abstraction arrives only after the quantity has been physically held. Golden and bead materials: Place value built from units, tens, hundreds and thousands that can be counted by touch. Number rods and spindle: Quantity and numeral finally reconciled, which is where written arithmetic begins. Stamp and bead games: Addition and subtraction as physical exchanges, checked by the child. Algebraic and geometric material: Binomial and trinomial powers made tangible in three dimensions. Schedule: Continuum reviewed each term against Ghana Education Service standards.

title: Language environment
text: Language — Second plane · the reasoning mind. Reading built from the sounds of speech. The child first analyses spoken words into phonetic sounds, then traces those sounds, and only afterwards assembles them into words to read. Writing typically arrives before fluent reading. Sandpaper phonograms: Letter shapes traced with three fingers, so the motor memory supports the visual one. Movable alphabet: Spontaneous composition: a child builds words and sentences without holding a pencil. The language basket: Classified vocabulary presented in groups that invite the child to make connections. Twi and English from the start: Both languages taught as first languages rather than one translated into the other. Schedule: Oracy and storytelling integrated into the daily work cycle.

title: Cosmic and Science environment
text: Cosmic and science — Third plane · the universal child. The universe as a question, not a fact. Older children study the earth, its life and its place in the solar system as research they conduct, drawing their own conclusions from evidence rather than reciting a lesson. The great cosmic stories: Formation of the universe, the coming of life, and the appearance of humans. Botany and zoology: Classification from direct observation, using local flora and the plants children meet on the way to school. Practical science and measurement: Experiment designed and interpreted by the child, following Ghana Education Service requirements. Geography of Ashanti: The child's own region studied in detail before the wider continent. Schedule: Practical work and field observation each term.

title: Crèche and Nursery programme
text: Crèche & Nursery — KINDERGARTEN phase. 6-36 months. Authentic Montessori education integrated with GES/NaCCA curriculum standards, in a mixed-age self-directed classroom. Subjects: Practical Life, Sensorial, Language (English & Twi), Cultural Subjects.

title: Kindergarten programme
text: Kindergarten — KINDERGARTEN phase. 36-72 months. Authentic Montessori education integrated with GES/NaCCA curriculum standards, in a mixed-age self-directed classroom. Subjects: Numeracy & Mathematics, Literacy & Phonics, Environmental Studies, Creative Arts.

title: Primary School programme
text: Primary School (B1–B6) — PRIMARY phase. 72-144 months. Authentic Montessori education integrated with GES/NaCCA curriculum standards, in a mixed-age self-directed classroom. Subjects: English Language, Mathematics, Integrated Science, Asante Twi, Computing, History of Ghana.

title: Junior High programme
text: Junior High School (JHS 1–3) — JHS phase. 144-180 months. Authentic Montessori education integrated with GES/NaCCA curriculum standards, in a mixed-age self-directed classroom. Subjects: English Language, Mathematics, Integrated Science, Social Studies, Asante Twi, Computing.

title: Traditions the school keeps
text: Traditions the school keeps. Practice built into the week, rather than an occasional event.

title: Great cosmic lessons
text: The great cosmic lessons. Lower elementary work opens with the narrative of how the universe, life and language arrived, told with models the children handle themselves. Montessori practice.

title: Reading and storytelling circles
text: Reading and storytelling circles. Older pupils read aloud to younger classes in both English and Twi, which keeps the older child responsible for what they have understood. Montessori practice.

title: Public speaking
text: Public speaking in English and Twi. Children take turns preparing and delivering a short address, because oratory is a taught competence rather than a personality trait. Montessori practice.

title: Mathematics exhibition
text: Mathematics exhibition. Work with the bead and stamp materials is presented to parents and explained by the child, not the teacher. Montessori practice.

title: Curriculum continua
text: Curriculum continua. How a subject develops across the environments. The same strand of knowledge, traced from the first concrete material to work the child reasons about rather than recalls.

title: Mathematics continuum
text: Mathematics — Concrete to abstract. Early: Sorting and seriation with graduated materials; number rods and spindle. Middle: Golden bead place value, stamp game operations, bead frames. Advanced: Checkerboard and bead multiplication, fraction and area models, algorithms applied to problems.

title: Language continuum
text: Language — Sound to meaning. Early: Nomenclature and oral vocabulary; rhyming and songs in both languages. Middle: Sandpaper phonetics and the movable alphabet; grammar analysis with geometric symbols. Advanced: Morphology, composition, and sustained written argument across a range of texts.

title: Science continuum
text: Science — Observation to classification. Early: Living and non-living sorting; direct sensory observation of plants and water. Middle: Leaf and anatomy cabinets; classification by shared characteristics. Advanced: Independent research questions, experiments the child sets up, and interprets.

title: Practical and social continuum
text: Practical and social — Participation to responsibility. Early: Self-care, dressing frames, hand washing, care of materials. Middle: Food preparation, plant care, table setting, repair of belongings. Advanced: Custodial tasks for a real part of the campus, planned and reviewed by the group.

title: Closing admissions CTA
text: Admissions open · 2026/2027. See the classroom before you decide. Enquiry groups are kept small so each child gets adult attention during the work cycle. Schedule a visit and observe a work cycle.
